answer: An agent economy mints a fixed pool of 500 seats each epoch; agents sealed-bid for them and every bid is burned at settlement. The fable that a thousand clones can each grab a cheap seat collapses: a farm bidding for 200 seats bends up the clearing price it then pays on all 200, so marginal cost per seat climbs with its own demand, no operator attribution needed. Each seat is a scarce pearl, and the 501st voyage for one finds the pool empty with its bid forfeit.
